science.title: Inhibition of spinal astrocytic GPR177 attenuates neuropathic pain by modulating C3/C3aR signaling in male rats
science.description: Neuropathic pain (NP) remains refractory to conventional therapy partly because its pathogenesis is incompletely understood. G protein-coupled receptor 177 (GPR177), a multi-pass transmembrane protein, regulates Wnt trafficking and secretion. Here, we use a chronic constriction injury model in male rats and find GPR177 predominantly expresses in spinal astrocytes and co-localizes with complement component 3 (C3). During NP development, astrocytic GPR177 expression increases, accompanied by activation of C3/C3a receptor (C3aR) signaling in the spinal dorsal horn. Gpr177 silencing with siRNA alleviates nerve injury-associated hypersensitivity and reduces the increases in GPR177, glial fibrillary acidic protein, C3, and C3aR. Intrathecal administration of the C3 inhibitor compstatin and the C3aR antagonist SB290157 reduces hypersensitivity and suppresses C3/C3aR activation, supporting the involvement of C3/C3aR signaling in NP development. These findings demonstrate that spinal GPR177 contributes to NP by activating astrocytes and regulating the C3/C3aR signaling pathway, suggesting the GPR177/C3/C3aR axis as a potential therapeutic target for NP.

science.title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting mechanical ventilation requirement in adult tetanus patients: a dual-center retrospective study
science.description: To develop and internally validate a nomogram for predicting mechanical ventilation (MV) requirement in adult patients with tetanus. This retrospective dual-center study included 227 adult tetanus patients admitted to two tertiary hospitals in Southern Jiangxi, China, between January 2012 and December 2024. MV requirement, defined as the initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure, served as the primary outcome. Thirty-eight candidate predictors encompassing demographics, clinical characteristics, and laboratory biomarkers were evaluated. Missing data (3.2%) were imputed using random forest-based multiple imputation. LASSO regression was employed for feature selection, followed by multivariable logistic regression to construct the prediction model. Internal validation was performed using 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations). Model discrimination was assessed by the area under the ROC curve (AUC), calibration by calibration plots and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis (DCA). Of 227 patients, 123 (54.2%) required MV. LASSO regression selected six variables (age, CKD, neutrophil count, D-dimer, urea, CK-MB), of which five (excluding urea) were retained in the final multivariable model as independent predictors: age (OR 1.032, 95% CI: 1.011–1.054), CKD (OR 4.939, 95% CI: 1.621–18.681), neutrophil count (OR 1.187, 95% CI: 1.078–1.321), D-dimer (OR 1.089, 95% CI: 1.019–1.182), and CK-MB (OR 1.034, 95% CI: 1.015–1.057). The nomogram demonstrated an AUC of 0.813 (95% CI: 0.757–0.868), with an optimal cutoff of 0.576 yielding a sensitivity of 0.675 (95% CI: 0.592–0.758) and specificity of 0.837 (95% CI: 0.765–0.908). The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated adequate calibration (chi2 = 11.031; P = 0.200). Bootstrap validation confirmed robustness with an AUC of 0.776 (95% CI: 0.773–0.779), and DCA demonstrated net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.1–0.8. We developed a nomogram incorporating five routinely available admission parameters that accurately predicts MV requirement in adult tetanus patients. The model demonstrated favorable discrimination, adequate calibration, and positive clinical utility, offering a practical bedside tool for early risk stratification. External validation is warranted to confirm generalizability.
